name: Bengali
variety: Standard Colloquial Bengali; the inventory covers both the Kolkata and the Dhaka standard, the formant, duration, VOT and intonation figures come from Bangladeshi Standard (Dhaka) speakers
sources: Khan, Sameer ud Dowla (2010). Bengali (Bangladeshi Standard). Journal of the International Phonetic Association 40(2), 221-225.
Ferguson, Charles A. & Chowdhury, Munier (1960). The phonemes of Bengali. Language 36, 22-59.
Dasgupta, Probal (2003). Bangla. In Cardona, George & Jain, Dhanesh (eds.), The Indo-Aryan Languages. London: Routledge.
Chatterji, Suniti Kumar (1921). Bengali phonetics. Bulletin of the School of Oriental Studies 2, 1-25.
Masica, Colin P. (1991). The Indo-Aryan Languages. Cambridge University Press.
Hayes, Bruce & Lahiri, Aditi (1991). Bengali intonational phonology. Natural Language & Linguistic Theory 9, 47-96.

Khan, Sameer ud Dowla (2014). The intonational phonology of Bangladeshi Standard Bengali. In Jun, Sun-Ah (ed.), Prosodic Typology II: The Phonology of Intonation and Phrasing. Oxford University Press.
Khan, Sameer ud Dowla (2008). Intonational Phonology and Focus Prosody of Bengali. PhD dissertation, University of California, Los Angeles.
Mikuteit, Simone & Reetz, Henning (2007). Caught in the ACT: the timing of aspiration and voicing in East Bengali. Language and Speech 50(2), 247-277.
Alam, Firoj; Habib, S. M. Murtoza & Khan, Mumit (2008). Acoustic analysis of Bangla vowel inventory. Technical report, Center for Research on Bangla Language Processing, BRAC University, Dhaka.
Lahiri, Aditi & Hankamer, Jorge (1988). The timing of geminate consonants. Journal of Phonetics 16, 327-338.
Berkson, Kelly Harper (2012). Capturing breathy voice: durational measures of oral stops in Marathi. Kansas Working Papers in Linguistics 33, 27-46 (tabulates the Mikuteit & Reetz values).

vowel_formants.speaker: adult male (mean of 3 speakers aged 25-29, Dhaka; target words in a carrier sentence)

contrasts: four-way laryngeal contrast in stops and affricates: voiceless unaspirated, voiceless aspirated, voiced, breathy voiced
seven vowel qualities with /e/ : /æ/ and /o/ : /ɔ/, contrastive mainly in the first syllable
oral versus nasal vowels in the Kolkata standard (/kãʈa/ 'thorn' : /kaʈa/ 'to cut'); weak or absent in Bangladeshi Standard
/ɾ/ versus /ɽ/ in the Kolkata standard; one rhotic in most Bangladeshi speech
/ʃ/ versus /s/, marginal in Kolkata, regular in Dhaka (/bas/ 'enough' : /baʃ/ 'bamboo')
allophony: regressive height assimilation: /ɔ/ is [o] and /æ/ is [e] when the next syllable has /i/ or /u/ (/kɔɾ-i/ [koɾi] 'I do' beside [kɔɾe] 'does')
/ʃ/ is [s] before dental and alveolar consonants (/st̪ri/, /snan/, /sri/)
/pʰ/ is [f] or [ɸ] for most speakers; /bʱ/ may be [β] or [v]; /dʒ/ is [z] in many eastern accents
the 'retroflex' stops are apical postalveolar, less retracted than in Hindi or Marathi; the affricates are laminal dorso-alveolar
the rhotic is an approximant or a tap, devoiced in codas; consonants lengthen after it
/ɦ/ is weak or lost between vowels
vowels are longer in monosyllabic words and at the end of a phrase
final stops are unreleased; breathy voiced stops lose breathiness word-finally
off-glides of diphthongs are higher than the corresponding full vowels
syllable_structure: (C)(C)(C)V(C)(C); native words are (C)V(C), clusters occur in Sanskrit and English loans (/st̪ri/ 'wife')
phonotactics: the inherent vowel is /ɔ/ or /o/; whether it is pronounced word-finally and after medial consonants is lexical and not shown in the script (/bʱat̪/ 'rice' but /tʃʰoʈo/ 'small')
written conjuncts with ya-phala, ba-phala and ma-phala are pronounced as geminates: সত্য [ʃot̪ːo], বিশ্ব [biʃːo], পদ্ম [pɔd̪ːo]
ক্ষ is [kʰ] initially and [kːʰ] medially; জ্ঞ is [ɡ] or [ɡː] with a fronted following vowel (জ্ঞান [ɡæn])
/ŋ/ and /ɽ/ do not occur word-initially; /ɖ ɖʱ/ are rare after vowels inside morphemes
the letter এ stands for /e/ or /æ/ and the inherent vowel for /ɔ/ or /o/ without any mark

stress.rule: The first syllable of the word is prominent.
stress.cues: phonetically not salient; the prominent syllable carries the low pitch accent of the rising accentual phrase and licenses the full set of vowel contrasts; little duration or intensity difference

rhythm.vowel_reduction: none in quality; fewer vowel contrasts outside the first syllable
rhythm.notes: Final syllables are lengthened at intermediate-phrase and intonation-phrase boundaries but not at accentual-phrase boundaries (Khan 2014). No nPVI value could be verified.

length.notes: Vowel length is not contrastive. In carrier-sentence words monophthongs last about 68-98 ms and diphthongs about 140-195 ms (means over 6 speakers, Alam, Habib & Khan 2008). Geminate stops have about twice the closure duration of singletons or more (Lahiri & Hankamer 1988).

voice_onset_time_ms.source: Mikuteit & Reetz 2007 (East Bengali; after-closure time, least-square means), as tabulated in Berkson 2012
voice_onset_time_ms.notes: For voiceless stops the after-closure time equals VOT. Voiced and breathy voiced stops are prevoiced; their lag from release to regular periodic voicing is b 8, d̪ 13, ɖ 7, ɡ 23 and bʱ 31, d̪ʱ 35, ɖʱ 36, ɡʱ 44 ms. Breathy voice superimposed on the vowel lasts about 47 ms after breathy voiced stops and about 24 ms after voiceless aspirates. No value for /pʰ/, which is a fricative in this variety.

intonation.declarative: a chain of accentual phrases (content word plus clitics), each with a low pitch accent on the first syllable and a high boundary on the last (L* ... Ha), peaks declining; the final phrase falls from its accent to a low boundary (L%), often with creaky voice
intonation.yes_no_question: pitch rises steadily from the last accent to the start of the final syllable, which then falls sharply (HL%); confirmation questions end in a plain high rise (H%)
intonation.wh_question: focus on the wh-word (raised rise, compression after it) and a low boundary (L%); when little is shared a rising boundary (LH%)
intonation.continuation: high boundary at the end of each non-final accentual phrase; larger rise (H-) at intermediate phrase ends; non-final clauses end in LH% or the dipping HLH%
intonation.accent_shape: L* ... Ha: low on the word-initial syllable, peak on the last syllable of the accentual phrase; under focus L*+H with the peak on the second syllable
intonation.notes: Khan 2014 (Bangladeshi Standard); Hayes & Lahiri 1991 give a closely similar analysis of Kolkata Bengali with L* HP phrases and a final HL sequence in yes/no questions.

phonation: breathy voiced (murmured) stops and affricates /bʱ d̪ʱ ɖʱ dʒʱ ɡʱ/
breathiness is carried by the release and the first part of the vowel
creaky voice at low final boundaries

problems: Breathy voiced stops come from the Hindi base table: modal voiced closure plus a voiceless aspiration sample, no breathy vowel onset. /ɦ/ is voiceless [h].
The final inherent vowel is often wrong in both directions: ভাত [bʰato], হয় [hɔjo] with an extra vowel, ছোট [tʃʰoʈ], বড় [bɔɽ] without the needed final [o].
The letter এ is always [e]: এক [ek], দেখা [dekʰa] for [æk], [d̪ækʰa].
Conjuncts are read letter by letter: বিশ্ব [biʃbɔ], পদ্ম [pɔdmɔ], আত্মা [atma], ক্ষতি [kʰkʰoti], লক্ষ্মী [lokʰkʰmi], জ্ঞান [ɡɡan].
One phoneme /dʒ/ has two sounds: জ is the palatal stop phoneme [ɟ], য is [dʒ].
ঢ় is produced as [h] followed by the retroflex flap (আষাঢ় [aʃahɽɔ]); the flap has no IPA name and prints as 'r.'.
/ʃ/ stays [ʃ] before dentals and /r/ in স্নান [ʃnan], শ্রী [ʃɾi].
Raising of the inherent vowel to [o] is applied only in the first syllable.
Intonation uses the generic eSpeak tunes: no rising accentual phrases, no rise-fall on the last syllable of yes/no questions.
good: no vowel length contrast; seven vowel qualities including [æ] and [ɔ]
the inherent vowel is [o] before /i u/ in the next syllable (কবি [kobi], করি [koɾi]) and [ɔ] otherwise
gemination from ya-phala in সত্য, অন্য

notes: /f z/ are loan or variant phonemes and /ɽʱ/ is marginal (merged with /ɽ/ by most speakers). Glides are treated as non-syllabic vowels in diphthongs. The diphthong list follows Khan 2010 and Alam et al. 2008; counts in the literature range from 17 to 31.
